classification_theorem.balanced: if N is even and k=N/2, the periodic core is exactly the two alternating states, both of period two
classification_theorem.high_density: if k>=N/2, a state is periodic iff it has no cyclic 00; on that core F is left rotation
classification_theorem.low_density: if k<=N/2, a state is periodic iff it has no cyclic 11; on that core F is right rotation
classification_theorem.period_divisibility: every temporal least period divides N and equals the least cyclic rotation period
classification_theorem.uniform: k=0 and k=N each contain one fixed uniform state

finite_attraction_theorem.bound: every state reaches the isolated-minority periodic core in at most m^2 updates
finite_attraction_theorem.duality: the high-density proof exchanges particles with left-moving holes
finite_attraction_theorem.lyapunov: the number of zero minority gaps never increases and, while positive, decreases within at most m updates
finite_attraction_theorem.zero_marker_rule: a zero gap shifts one index backward unless its predecessor is at least two, in which case that zero is absorbed

fixed_and_primitive_theorem.fixed_count: with m=min(k,N-k), g=gcd(N,n), q=N/g: #Fix(F^n|X_(N,k))=I(g,m/q) if q divides m, and zero otherwise
fixed_and_primitive_theorem.independent_cycle_count: I(g,0)=1; I(g,r)=g/(g-r)*binom(g-r,r) for 1<=r<=floor(g/2), and zero otherwise

koopman_boundary.periodic_core: restriction to the canonical periodic core is a finite rotation permutation and has a natural unitary Koopman operator
koopman_boundary.reversal: spatial reflection reverses the core rotation, but the core restriction discards full-system transients
koopman_boundary.transient_boundary: when m>=2 the sector contains transient states, so the whole-sector uniform Koopman composition operator is not unitary
koopman_boundary.whole_sector: the whole-sector map is bijective exactly when m<=1; then it is a cyclic rotation

nonclaims: external novelty or priority for the classical Rule-184 facts
prime semantics for traffic cycles or their repetitions
unitarity of the full sector when transient states are present
a target divisor, functional equation, counting law, continuation, or Weil compression
arithmetic local factors, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, a Hilbert--Polya operator, Route-B authorization, or external peer review

progress_and_boundary.progress: proves the all-N all-density periodic-core classification, finite attraction, every iterate fixed count, primitive-cycle product, and exact full-versus-core Koopman boundary
progress_and_boundary.route_a_obstruction: the cycles are intrinsic but carry no arithmetic semantics, target divisor comparison, or target global analytic structure
progress_and_boundary.sentinel_boundary: finite enumeration regression-tests formulas proved combinatorially and does not extrapolate the infinite family

source_lock.allowed_data: the frozen local rule, N, k, cyclic adjacency, gcd, binomial and Mobius arithmetic
source_lock.arithmetic_origin: none; particle number and traffic motion have no intrinsic prime or prime-power semantics
source_lock.cutoff: all-parameter proof; exhaustive regression for 1<=N<=12 and 1<=n<=2N+2
source_lock.determinant_convention: Artin--Mazur zeta of the finite sector and the finite periodic-core Koopman determinant
source_lock.family: every N>=1 and every fixed particle sector 0<=k<=N
source_lock.forbidden_data: target zero or prime tables, arithmetic local data, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, Hilbert--Polya operators, and Route-B inputs
source_lock.normalization: labelled cyclic sites; right shift has (rho x)_i=x_(i-1)
source_lock.object: cyclic elementary cellular automaton Rule 184 on binary words of length N
source_lock.precision: exact binary states and integer counts
